title: On the Origin of Algorithmic Progress in AI: Evidence from Language Model Pre-Training
abstract: arXiv:2511.21622v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Algorithms have been estimated to increase AI pretraining FLOP efficiency by a factor of 22,000 between 2012 and 2023 (Ho et al., 2024). Running ablation experiments on key innovations from this time period, we are able to account for less than 10x of these gains at small compute scales. Surveying the broader literature, we estimate that additional innovations not included in our ablations also account for less than 10x, yielding less than 100x efficiency gains total in low-compute regimes. This leads us to conduct scaling experiments, which provide evidence that the efficiency gap can be explained by algorithms with scale-dependent efficiency improvements. In particular, we conduct scaling experiments between LSTMs and Transformers, finding evidence for exponent differences in their compute-optimal scaling law while finding little scaling difference for many other innovations. translated_title: 论AI算法进步之源：来自语言模型预训练的证据
translated_abstract: 据估计，在2012年至2023年间，算法使AI预训练的FLOP效率提升了22,000倍（Ho et al., 2024）。通过对该时期关键创新开展消融实验，我们在小算力规模下只能解释其中不到10倍的收益。在调研更广泛的文献后，我们估计未纳入消融实验的其他创新的贡献同样不足10倍，因此在低算力区间，总效率提升不足100倍。这促使我们开展缩放实验，实验证据表明，这一效率差距可以由具有规模依赖性效率提升的算法来解释。具体而言，我们在LSTM与Transformer之间进行了缩放实验，发现了二者在计算最优缩放律上存在指数差异的证据，而许多其他创新则几乎没有表现出缩放差异。这些实验表明，与标准假设相反……
tldr: 该论文通过消融与缩放实验发现，2012–2023年间AI预训练约22,000倍的算法效率提升无法由小算力下的各项具体创新解释，而主要源于Transformer等算法随规模增大而增强的效率优势。
en_tdlr: This paper shows through ablation and scaling experiments that the estimated 22,000x algorithmic efficiency gains in AI pretraining (2012–2023) cannot be explained by specific innovations at small compute scales, but mainly arise from algorithms like Transformers whose efficiency advantages grow with scale.
